messages:
ajay: Quick Q — are we comfortable with the current behavior where premium tenants get strict region affinity while standard tenants get simple failover? I'm worried about tail latency spikes when the preferred region flaps.

maria: I think strict affinity helps data locality for enterprise, but it does increase outage blast radius. For premium we could try hedging rather than strict stickiness. hedging = send duplicate to fallback if primary > X ms.

kevin: Two constraints: 1) model-variant compatibility (fp16 vs int8) and 2) quota accounting. If we hedge across region we might bill double tokens for one request. Need clear billing semantics.

olivia: UX ask — console should show "fallback risk" per route + expected delta in token billing if hedging is enabled. customers should opt-in.

ajay: prototype policy I sketched (pseudo-yaml):
```
routing_policy:
  tenant_tier: premium
  region_affinity: true
  hedging:
    enabled: true
    threshold_ms: 50
    max_forks: 1
  fallback:
    allow_variant_downgrade: true
    variant_priority: ["v2-fp16", "v2-int8", "v2-quant"]
    preserve_kv_cache: false
```

kevin: If allow_variant_downgrade=true we must tag responses with variant metadata and surface that in logs/telemetry. Also add automatic quality regression alert if downstream evals drop.

probe-bot: probe eu-west p50=38ms p95=130ms, us-west p50=82ms p95=210ms, ap-south p50=290ms p95=600ms

maria: Given those probes, hedging threshold 50ms would trigger fallback for many requests from us-west -> eu-west. That reverses the usual flow. We should base decision on client latency (client->region) + intra-region SLO.

ajay: Right — idea: compute effective_latency = client_rtt + region_probe_penalty. route to region with min(effective_latency + tier_penalty). Tier_penalty for non-premium = +40ms, premium=0. Allows premium to prefer latency but still fallback.

olivia: For console rollout UX: show a "Simulate routing" button where you can drop in an IP or region and see which region + variant would be chosen and expected cost delta. Also a per-route toggle: "allow variant downgrade" with a tooltip.

kevin: API debate: should the routing decision be deterministic server-side (single region pick) or returned as a ranked list to client so client can retry hedged choices? Pros/cons?

ajay: I prefer server-side decision with optional hedging. Returning ranked list leaks internal topology and complicates client. But server-side needs robust telemetry for retries/duplicates.

maria: On quotas: if hedging duplicates count toward quota, we need a "hedged_token_multiplier" that is visible in billing preview. If we don't count duplicates, we need dedup and idempotency guarantees which are harder across regions.

probe-bot: recent anomaly: eu-west 5min window had 12% p95 spike, ejection threshold crossed twice. note: several tenants on dedicated pools were routed out.

olivia: Can we add a console alert rule generator: "if region ejects > X for Y mins, notify tenants with affinity and suggest temporary allow_variant_downgrade"?

kevin: Implementation note — kv-cache preservation across variants is tricky. If variant changes architecture or tokenizers, reusing cache could produce corruption. Need explicit compatibility matrix.

ajay: Agreed. So fallback policy must include a compatibility check step. If incompatible -> either reject fallback or do cold-start without cache and with a warning.

maria: For rollout: we should permit canary routing rules per-tenant. Example: canary 5% traffic to new fallback-policy for group A. UI shows per-tenant rollout % and observed latency/cost delta.

deploy-bot: canary rollout: region-routing-v2 -> 5% tenants (started by ajay)

ajay: Next actions: 1) kevin to draft variant-compatibility matrix & telemetry fields (variant_id, fallback_reason, hedged=true, billed_tokens), 2) olivia to sketch console mock for "simulate routing" and "fallback risk", 3) maria to write proposal for tier_penalty model and hedging thresholds.

kevin: I'll push a small protobuf change for response metadata tomorrow with backwards compat.

olivia: I'll put a prototype mock in Figma then ping for review.

ajay: Thanks — if anyone wants to join a quick sync after standup, 10 mins to align on API shape.

maria: dropping a couple notes into the design doc after sync. :white_check_mark:
